title: Chapter 567
paragraphs: Chapter 567
Episode 147. The King of the Black Sea, Gliek (11)
'What is this...!'
Everywhere he looked, there was only a grim darkness.
The sharp noise that occurred as the Great Ice Field shattered, the voices of those reacting to the suddenly changed situation, and the sound of debris, sword energy, and magic colliding.
He couldn't hear anything.
The sensation of being isolated from the world without a moment to realize or resist made his nerves tense, but all he felt was the empty energy unique to this black space.
For a moment, Jin even had the illusion that he was dead, but he held onto his composure.
'It seems I've been pulled into Gliek's subspace.'
He raised his hand and looked at his sword. In the pitch darkness, only Jin's body and belongings maintained their original colors.
Jin had been in a space almost identical to this before.
'It's almost identical to Solderet's subspace. Clearly, there's a profound connection between spirit energy and the power of chaos that I don't know. It's uncomfortably similar.'
The darkness formed by Gliek resembled the subspace of shadows. It was almost identical in every aspect except for one.
Whether the space was friendly or hostile to him.
In Solderet's subspace, there was a strangely unfamiliar yet comforting feeling, but the current darkness was full of indescribably immense hostility.
And that hostility wasn't just staring at Jin.
He began to feel that some invisible, creepy, and cold force was infiltrating his entire body.
"Ugh!"
It felt as if a frozen blade was tearing his flesh and piercing his bones.
His fist reflexively clenched and a groan escaped from his tightly closed mouth.
Chaos.
What was causing Jin such pain was chaos imbued with Gliek's will.
This force was far surpassing all the physical and mental pain Jin had endured so far.
If he hadn't had a strong mind, honed by crossing the line of death many times, Jin wouldn't have lasted even 5 minutes.
"Ugh, cough..."
Even for Jin.
He had no choice but to be soaked in fear. There were no allies in this dark space to help him, and he couldn't imagine escaping from here alone.
A feeling he had never contemplated even when fighting against the imperial army or Zipfel's grand army was trying to take over Jin.
'Damn it, my hand...!'
Suddenly, Jin staggered backward in shock.
He saw his fingertips, which were holding the sword, being dyed black by chaos.
It was an experience he'd never had before, but he could recognize it immediately. This terrible discoloration was the result of being corroded by chaos.
His back felt cold and it seemed like his blood was cooling.
Upon closer inspection, the chaotic energy that dyed one joint of his index finger seemed to be growing. It was crawling like a caterpillar.
Moreover, the corrosion didn't just start from the tip of his fingers.
All the places where the pain was particularly severe were the points where the corrosion was taking place.
What happens when the corrosion is complete?
The conclusion he intuitively reached was a future where he becomes part of Gliek, just as Dante had.
He had to overcome it.
'It's fundamentally no different from the despair I've always overcome, only the size and depth are different. I'll somehow stop the corrosion and find a way out of here.'
He raised his head, put all his strength into it, and stood up.
But as soon as he took a step, he fell over, and it happened five times.
Jin concluded that it was impossible for him to walk in this state.
Just as no one can walk with a severed leg, Jin couldn't move forward now. It was something he could never resist with willpower alone.
So, Jin sat down. He didn't slump down, but sat cross-legged and focused his mind.
Spirit energy release.
He felt he had to push out the spreading chaos in his body with it. Shadows engulfed in chaos were rising following Jin's spirit energy release.
Fortunately, it had an effect. The released spirit energy was washing away the chaos like clear water.
There was hope. If one didn't possess the power of Genesis, the only one who could glimpse the possibility of escape in this way in Gliek's subspace was the contractor of shadows.
There were two problems.
Firstly, he couldn't stably release spirit energy as usual due to the pain.
Although it should have been pouring out like a waterfall to completely end the corrosion, the power of the shadow was only responding weakly.
Secondly, there was another phenomenon that occurred as soon as the spirit energy release began.
The unpushed chaos was trying to 'mix' with the spirit energy. It was as if it was a stream of water returning to its source.
'There's nothing easy in this damn war and fight from one to ten.'
The spirit energy mixed with chaos was getting out of Jin's control.
Also, it became stronger. Except for the clear will of Solderet during the first battle, Jin had never seen a spirit energy more intensely fluctuating than this.
It was similar to when the spirit energy mixed with aura and magic and enhanced them. It was just hard to control, like a raging beast.
The spirit energy release was weak, and the shadows mixed with chaos were explosive.
There was no reason not to use it, even if it was dangerous.
"Perhaps this too could be another trap set by Gliek, but I have no other choice. With the pure spirit energy of Spirit Liberation alone, all I can do is delay the erosion."
Jin's choice was no different from throwing himself into turbulent waters, not knowing where they might lead.
However, he somehow felt a surge of confidence.
The attribute of chaos that enhances spirit energy.
He had a thought that this could be a deliberate design of the entity that created this principle. Perhaps it is the will of Solderet, the god.
I will make this power my own.
Spirit energy began to move according to Jin's will.
The flow was quickening not just out of vague resistance to chaos for survival, but because a milestone called 'struggle' had been set.
He suppressed the excessively turbulent spirit energy and gripped the merely growing masses.
Rebellion from chaos made blood rise relentlessly in his throat, and occasionally consciousness faded, but Jin was certain.
The fact that his body, which had been trampled by pain, was gradually improving.
No, it was more than just that. Although unstable, a power beyond his limit seemed about to burst forth at any moment.
Around then, Jin noticed that another inherent power within him, not spirit energy, was reacting to chaos.
Blood.
The Divine Blood, which not only recognized him but also made part of the physical nature of Jin Runcandel, the human being, as the same as his brothers, was fiercely driving chaos.
"Seems like devouring is not only permitted for you, Gliek!"
Fzzzzzzzzzzz...!
Lightning mixed between spirit energy and chaos. As if not afraid of erosion, his blood was rather drawing all the chaos it caught into a crazed heart.
Soon, Jin sat up straight, releasing his cross-legged position.
Though his shoulders still felt heavy as if trapped underwater, the pain eased a lot when he started walking slowly.
With each step forward, the spirit energy, which had been turbulent mixing with chaos, found its place.
After taking seven steps, Jin was able to feel that he had overcome the first trial of this subspace.
The erosion had stopped, and Jin was no longer in pain.
The chaos that had been so violently raging mixed with the spirit energy twitched faintly like a weak pulse.
And his body, which had been worn out from the long fight, was now filled with a power stronger than before the war began. It felt as if there was nothing in the world he couldn't cut.
"Did I temporarily grow by overcoming chaos? Or... is this some kind of side effect?"
He couldn't immediately tell.
Given the traces of discoloration left all over his body, there would be a cost to pay one way or another.
Jin also realized that his fighting spirit was burning excessively. This was completely opposite to his intention to maintain composure as much as possible.
"If I can't make it completely mine, it's a dangerous power. Now that the physical erosion has stopped, it seems to be trying to destroy my mind."
"The target of the chaos's erosion has shifted from the body to the mind," Jin concluded, as his youngest niece, Yona, had done.
He could not guarantee that he could overcome this again. Neither Spirit Liberation nor Divine Blood could directly protect the mind.
He had to find an exit while he could still maintain his rationality as much as possible.
The situation outside was one of two things. They were either trying to save Jin, or they were fighting Gliek.
He tried not to worry, though it was a concern.
He had no room to spare just suppressing the surging fighting spirit and lust for life.
The front was still dark, and all he could hear was his own breathing and the small noises caused by the electric aura emanating from his Divine Blood.
He swirled around with the spirit energy strengthened by Bradamante. Despite his confidence that there would be nothing he could not cut, the subspace remained unaffected.
No matter how many times he tried, the result was the same, so Jin had only one choice. He could only keep walking until something else appeared.
And in the vast expanse of subspace, Jin met something other than darkness faster than expected.
"A person...!?"
Although it appeared dim and dark, he saw the figure of a person huddled in a part of the darkness in the distance.
Jin hurriedly walked towards the figure, and soon he could recognize who it was.
"Captain Ron!"
He had not thought that someone else might have been dragged into this subspace. Especially Ron, who was not far from him.
'Then the others might also...!'
The moment Jin thought that far.
Ron raised his head and looked at him. And as soon as Jin made eye contact with him, he had to stop in his tracks.
Hostility filled with madness.
As deep and profound as the resentment he first felt from Gliek... it was because Ron's hatred was directed right at him.
"Captain Ron! It's Jin Runcandel. Don't you recognize me..."
"Why."
Ron interrupted Jin's words.
In that moment, Jin noticed that Ron's pupils were black as oil. He also realized that the reason was that he was eroded by chaos, which had been tormenting him until a moment ago.
Ron stood up and added these words.
"What this monster is aiming for is you... why, why did my grandson become its prey instead of you? Tell me, why was it the child who was sacrificed, not you..."
When Ron finished speaking, his Rasheed, stained black, was already touching Jin's throat.
